    – Java @Configuration scanner: Grep backend/src/main/java for @Configuration, @ConfigurationProperties, and @EnableConfigurationProperties classes (e.g. CacheConfig, SecurityConfig, KafkaConfig, TenantAwareDataSourceConfig). **Inventory:**

- `backend/pom.xml` — Maven build; no `<profiles>` (only a `shibboleth` repository id); plugins: spring-boot, compiler, surefire, jacoco (coverage check gate).
- `backend/Dockerfile` — backend container image (used by Render/Railway builds).
- `docker-compose.yml` / `.override.yml` / `.prod.yml` — local infra (Redis/Kafka/ES/PG), dev overrides, prod-like stack.
- `infra/monitoring/docker-compose.yml` — Prometheus/Grafana stack.
- `infra/deployment/kubernetes/*.yaml` — namespace, services, HPA, frontend/ES services.
- `infra/deployment/helm/hrms/` — Helm chart with `values-prod.yaml`/`values-staging.yaml`; `infra/deployment/kyverno/` — policy (no `:latest`).
- `render.yaml` — Render blueprint (free-tier tuned, schedulers off); Railway has **no config file** — it builds the Dockerfile with the `render` Spring profile (`application-render.yml`).
- CI: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `pr-validation.yml`, `deploy.yml`, `security-scan.yml`, `cosign-sign.yml` — all touch backend (build/test, PR gate, deploy, Trivy scans, image signing).

Aggregating sub-orchestrator findings into a verdict.

**GO** — backend configuration is fully inventoried, consistent across all three sub-teams, with no gaps or contradictions.

- **Spring properties**: `application.yml` (base, multi-document with dev/prod overlays) plus five profile files — `dev`, `prod`, `render` (Railway hosting), `test`, `demo` — and `logback-spring.xml` for logging.
- **Java config**: 36 `@Configuration`/`@ConfigurationProperties` classes covering security (JWT, SAML, cookies), data (JPA, read-replica routing, RLS-aware datasource), Redis/caching, Kafka/Elasticsearch/WebSocket, and integrations (Google Drive, Twilio, AI, email).
- **Build/deploy**: `pom.xml` (no Maven profiles), `backend/Dockerfile`, docker-compose variants, Helm chart with prod/staging values, K8s manifests, Kyverno policy, `render.yaml`; Railway uses the Dockerfile + `render` profile with no config file of its own.
- **One caveat**: secrets must remain env-driven in `application-prod.yml`/`application-render.yml` and CI workflow secrets — verified as currently the case.
